extraFacts.fact: Wave 4 products are API certified and supplied with the API monogram by API-licensed manufacturers to the applicable specification: API 6A, API 16A, API 16C, API 16D or API 7K.
NACE MR0175 / ISO 15156 sets material requirements for equipment used in H2S-containing oil and gas production.

API 6A product specification level (PSL 1 to 4) sets the inspection, testing and traceability applied; PR1 and PR2 are the performance requirement levels, PR2 having passed API 6A design-validation testing. PSL 3G adds a gas test.

faqs.q: What is a conventional frac surface test tree rated 10,000 psi used for?
faqs.a: A conventional frac surface test tree is a hydraulically actuated valve stack that controls and isolates a well during testing and well-service work. This 10,000 psi (10K) tree has 5 valves: 2 master, 1 swab, 2 wing, a 5-1/8 in vertical bore bore and standard-service valves. Cameron / FMC interchange. Permanent flanged variant for fixed installations.

faqs.q: What do the 5 valves on the conventional frac surface test tree do?
faqs.a: The tree carries 5 valves: 2 master, 1 swab, 2 wing. Master valves are the primary barrier, kept open in operation and closed to shut in; the swab valve gives wireline access above the master; the wing valves route flow to the choke manifold or flowback iron. Valve types: Hydraulic gate valves; manual gate (swab).

faqs.q: What are the end connections of the conventional frac surface test tree at 10,000 psi?
faqs.a: Top: API 6BX 10K studded. Bottom: API 6BX 10K studded. Lateral: 2× 1502 Female Weco. The top, bottom and lateral ends are different, so confirm each against the frac tree, choke manifold and flowback iron before ordering.

faqs.q: Should I choose the conventional frac 10,000 psi tree or the conventional frac 10,000 psi tree?
faqs.a: Choose by operation: this tree is for conventional frac work at 10,000 psi, while the conventional frac tree at 10,000 psi is built for conventional frac operations with 5 valves: 2 master, 1 swab, 2 wing. See the [Conventional Frac 1502 surface test tree](/p/surface-test-tree-conventional-frac-1502-10-000-psi-sour-service).

faqs.q: What are the pressure rating and actuation pressure of the conventional frac 10,000 psi surface test tree?
faqs.a: The working pressure is 10,000 psi (10K) on a 5-1/8 in vertical bore bore. Hydraulic actuation pressure is 3,000 psi pilot. The temperature class is P to API 6A.

faqs.q: Is the conventional frac 10,000 psi surface test tree standard or sour service, and what is its material class?
faqs.a: The conventional frac 10,000 psi tree is standard service, material class AA, so it is not offered here for H2S service. For sour wells ask for the sour-service version, such as the [conventional frac 1502 10,000 psi sour tree](/p/surface-test-tree-conventional-frac-1502-10-000-psi-sour-service). The temperature class is P.

faqs.q: Which API specification applies to the conventional frac 10,000 psi surface test tree?
faqs.a: The listing gives API 6A for the conventional frac 10,000 psi tree, and it is supplied by API-licensed manufacturers with the API certificate and monogram documentation issued with the order. Mill test reports to EN 10204 3.1 / 3.2 and hydrostatic body, seat and back-seat test certificates per unit are listed.

faqs.q: What does the conventional frac surface test tree connect to?
faqs.a: The conventional frac 10,000 psi tree connects to the frac or wellhead tree below and the choke manifold and flowback iron on the wings, through the listed ends (top: api 6bx 10k studded). Pair it with a matched-class [wellhead](/c/wellhead) and a [wellhead control panel](/c/wellhead-control-panels) for the pilot pressure; ring gaskets are in the [ring joint gasket range](/c/ring-joint-gaskets).

faqs.q: How is the conventional frac 10,000 psi surface test tree operated?
faqs.a: The master and wing valves are hydraulic gate valves driven by the pilot pressure (3,000 psi pilot), and the swab valve is manual. Close the master valves to shut in and check the hydraulic function on a test before the job. See the [wellhead components guide](/blog/wellhead-components-explained).

faqs.q: How does the conventional frac 10,000 psi tree differ from the conventional frac tree?
faqs.a: The conventional frac tree at 10,000 psi has 5 valves: 2 master, 1 swab, 2 wing, while the conventional frac tree at 10,000 psi has 5 valves: 2 master, 1 swab, 2 wing. Choose by the operation, because snubbing and coiled-tubing trees add a stripper or shear/seal BOP. See the [Conventional Frac 1502 surface test tree](/p/surface-test-tree-conventional-frac-1502-10-000-psi-sour-service).

faqs.q: How is the conventional frac 10,000 psi surface test tree operated?

faqs.q: What is an API 6A surface test tree (flowhead) used for?
faqs.a: Surface test trees (flowheads): 3-1/16" to 5-1/8", 3,000 to 20,000 psi, fail-close hydraulic flow wing with ESD, manual kill wing and swab valve, rotating sub, PSL 3 to 4.

faqs.q: What do PSL 1 to 4 and PR1 or PR2 mean on an API 6A surface test tree (flowhead)?
faqs.a: PSL is the product specification level and PR is the performance requirement. On the API 6A surface test tree (flowhead) the listing gives PSL 3 to 4; PR1 or PR2. A higher PSL adds inspection, testing and traceability, and PR2 valves have passed API 6A design-validation testing.

faqs.q: What sizes and pressure ratings does the API 6A surface test tree (flowhead) come in?
faqs.a: The listing covers 3-1/16" to 5-1/8" nominal bore at 3,000 to 20,000 psi working pressure, with aPI 6A flanged; hammer union; top sub thread. Give the bore, working pressure and end connection on the enquiry and we match the exact model.

faqs.q: What is the difference between a flowhead and a conventional frac surface test tree?
faqs.a: A flowhead is made for drill-stem and production well testing, carrying the string weight with a rotating sub. A conventional frac tree such as the [1502 15,000 psi frac test tree](/p/surface-test-tree-conventional-frac-1502-15-000-psi-standard-service) is for flowback control on a pumping spread.

faqs.q: How is the API 6A surface test tree (flowhead) tested?
faqs.a: For the API 6A surface test tree (flowhead) (3-1/16" to 5-1/8", 3,000 to 20,000 psi working pressure): hydrostatic tests to API 6A / 16A / 16C at the PSL ordered, with function tests of valves and controls. The test record is supplied with the valve. Shell and seat tests are proof tests and are never working pressures.

faqs.q: Which material and temperature classes does the API 6A surface test tree (flowhead) offer?
faqs.a: On the API 6A surface test tree (flowhead), body material is offered in API 6A material classes AA to HH (DD to HH for sour service), and the temperature range is API 6A temperature classes K to Y. For sour service the DD to HH classes apply to NACE MR0175 / ISO 15156. Give your temperature and H2S data on the enquiry.

faqs.q: Is the API 6A surface test tree (flowhead) to API specification, and what documents are supplied?

faqs.q: How is the API 6A surface test tree (flowhead) operated?

faqs.q: What does the rotating sub on a flowhead do?
faqs.a: The rotating sub lets the test string be turned to set packers while the flowhead stays connected to the surface lines. The top sub takes wireline lubricators and coiled tubing. See the [wellhead components guide](/blog/wellhead-components-explained).

faqs.q: Flowhead or frac surface test tree: which do I need for well testing?

faqs.q: What is a wellhead-mounted surface test tree rated 15,000 psi used for?

Master valves are the primary barrier, kept open in operation and closed to shut in; the swab valve gives wireline access above the master; the wing valves route flow to the choke manifold or flowback iron. Valve types: Hydraulic gates (master + wing); manual gate (swab).
